faq: Which stores can connect to the shop?
Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce and any store that can send a product feed. We choose the cleanest route for your platform and explain it before we start.
Can you promise my shop will be approved?
No. Meta decides on approval and may ask for more details. We prepare your business verification, policies and product data to meet the rules, and help you reply if they ask a question.
Does Meta charge fees for sales in the shop?
Fees depend on your selling method and region, and they are set by Meta, not by us. We show you where to read the current terms before you turn checkout on.
Do my products need special images?
Clear, well-lit photos on a plain or simple background are best, and Meta rejects some images with heavy text. We list any images that need replacing, and you can order design help.

desc:
Instagram and Facebook Shop setup connects your product catalog to Meta's apps so people can browse and buy where they already spend time. Ecom Swift LLC prepares the accounts, catalog and product data in your own accounts.

## What is an Instagram and Facebook Shop?

An Instagram and Facebook Shop is a storefront inside Meta's apps that shows your products from a connected catalog. People can browse collections, open product pages and tap tagged products in posts and stories. The purchase itself happens through the checkout method you choose, such as your own website or an in-app option where available.

## Why a shop on social channels helps buyers

Most people on social channels are not looking to shop at that moment. They are scrolling, and a product that appears in a post can catch their interest. If they must stop, search your website and find the item again, many will not bother. A shop shortens that path by placing the product, price and a buy route right where they found it.

A shop also gives your catalog a second shelf. Customers who never visit your website can still find and browse your products through your profile.

## Where setups usually go wrong

Most delays come from preparation, not from the idea. The business account may not be linked to the right page. The domain may not be verified. Product titles, prices, images or availability may be missing or may break the platform's rules. When a catalog contains errors, items are rejected, and the shop looks empty or partial.

Review is also part of the process. Meta decides whether a shop is approved, and nobody outside the company can promise the outcome. Careful preparation reduces avoidable problems, but it cannot override a decision.

## What a properly set up social shop includes

- A business account and page linked correctly to your profile.
- A commerce account connected to your store or catalog.
- Domain and business verification steps completed where required.
- Product data checked for titles, prices, images, links and stock.
- Rejected or flagged items fixed.
- Collections arranged so shoppers find products quickly.
- Product tags enabled on posts and stories.
- Return and shipping policy fields filled in.
- A checkout method chosen and tested.
- Launch posts with tagged products, and a test purchase in the fuller package.

## What we do

We begin with an audit of your accounts and your product feed. We check that your store platform can connect, link your accounts, fix common catalog problems and organize collections. Then we submit the shop for review and respond to any requests for changes that fall within our work.

The Basic package connects one catalog, sets up the commerce account, checks a first set of products and submits for review. The Standard package fixes a larger set of products, builds collections, enables product tags and sets up the checkout method. The Premium package covers the largest catalog size, adds launch posts with tagged products, tests a purchase from start to finish and includes a handover call. You can add more product fixes, collection ads setup or product tag training. Meta's fees and rules are set by Meta, and we advise you of those you need to know about.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep product titles, prices and stock accurate in your store.
- Use clear photos on a plain background.
- Write real shipping and return policies.
- Check that your domain and business details match.
- Tag products in posts only when they relate to the content.

**Avoid:**
- Listing products that platform rules do not allow.
- Using misleading prices, claims or photos.
- Uploading the same product many times with small changes.
- Sending shoppers to a page that does not match the listing.
- Resubmitting a rejected shop repeatedly without fixing the cause.

## Who this is for

This service suits an online store owner who already has a website and wants to sell through Instagram and Facebook. It suits a brand whose catalog was rejected and who needs the errors found and fixed. It also suits a seller with a strong social following who wants followers to browse the full range inside the app.

## What we need from you

We need access to your Meta business accounts, page and Instagram profile, given as an admin, partner or team user. We also need access to your store as a collaborator or staff user, so we can reach the products. We never need your passwords. Please send your store link, your policy details and any earlier rejection messages you received.
